title: How to cope with news overload, with Markus Brauer, PhD, and Don Grant, PhD

sentences.en: hurricanes, wildfires, and floods, school shootings, the pandemic, a youth mental health crisis, inflation and rising interest rates, the war in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 飓风、野火与洪水，校园枪击案，大流行，青少年心理健康危机，通货膨胀与不断上升的利率，乌克兰战争。

sentences.en: Some days it seems like all the news is bad.
sentences.zh: 有时候，似乎所有的消息都是坏消息。

sentences.en: And some days it seems that this media stream of death, doom, and destruction is unavoidable.
sentences.zh: 有时，似乎这种充满死亡、厄运和毁灭的媒体资讯流是不可避免的。

sentences.en: Are you suffering from news overload?
sentences.zh: 你是否正在遭受新闻过载的困扰？

sentences.en: Do you find yourself doom scrolling when you should be sleeping, eating, playing with your kids, or doing your job?
sentences.zh: 你是否发现自己本该睡觉、吃饭、陪孩子玩或工作时，却在疯狂刷手机浏览负面新闻？

sentences.en: Do you feel hounded by algorithms that keep sending you more bad news, not only to your social news feed, but to your email as well?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得算法如影随形，不仅把源源不断的坏消息推送给你的社交动态，还塞进你的邮箱？

sentences.en: Why is it so hard to shut off the news spigot even when it's only making you feel stressed, depressed, and anxious?
sentences.zh: 为什么关闭新闻水龙头这么难，哪怕它只会让你感到压力、沮丧和焦虑？

sentences.en: Is there anything you can do to control this constant barrage of news yet still be informed?
sentences.zh: 你是否有什么办法既能控制源源不断的新闻轰炸，又能保持对外界的了解？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that explores the connections between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: I have two guests today to talk about news media overload.
sentences.zh: 今天我有两位嘉宾来谈谈新闻媒体过载的话题。

sentences.en: Dr. Marcus Brower is professor of psychology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he directs the Brower Group Lab.
sentences.zh: 马库斯·布劳尔博士是威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的心理学教授，并在那里领导布劳尔集团实验室。

sentences.en: Research in his laboratory focuses on group and intergroup processes, including the consequences of belonging
sentences.zh: 他实验室的研究重点是群体和群际过程，包括归属感带来的后果

sentences.en: to high and low power groups, and how belonging to in-groups and out-groups affects people.
sentences.zh: 即属于高权力群体和低权力群体，以及归属内群体和外群体如何影响人们。

sentences.en: Dr. Brower is also a co-author of a 2021 study that found consuming news about the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with emotional distress, which we will talk about today.
sentences.zh: 布劳尔博士也是2008年一项研究的合著者之一，该研究发现，消费关于新冠疫情的新闻与情绪困扰有关，我们今天将对此进行讨论。

sentences.en: Our second guest is Dr. Don Grant, a media psychologist, researcher, and an addictions counselor with expertise in technology's impact on mental health.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二位嘉宾是唐·格兰特博士，他是一名媒体心理学家、研究员兼成瘾咨询师，在技术对心理健康的影响方面拥有专业知识。

sentences.en: He is president of APA's Division 46, the Society for Media Psychology and Technology.
sentences.zh: 他是美国心理学会第46分会（媒体心理学与技术学会）的主席。

sentences.en: He is also the national advisor of healthy device management for Newport Healthcare.
sentences.zh: 他还是纽波特医疗保健公司的健康设备管理国家顾问。

sentences.en: His research includes investigations into the potential effects of media exposure, social media, cyberbullying,
sentences.zh: 他的研究包括调查媒体曝光、社交媒体、网络霸凌的潜在影响，

sentences.en: and device-driven attachment bonds on adolescents, teens, and young adults, and our culture at large.
sentences.zh: 以及设备驱动的依恋纽带对青少年、少儿、年轻人以及整个文化的影响。

sentences.en: Welcome to both of you.
sentences.zh: 欢迎两位。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Kim.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，金。

sentences.en: Thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们来。

sentences.en: As I said just a moment ago, it feels like we're drowning in news, much of it disturbing, if not downright bad.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才所说，感觉我们被新闻淹没，其中大部分令人不安，甚至可以说是糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: Is it just my gut saying that there's so much news today that there's much, much more than there was, say, 10 years ago?
sentences.zh: 这只是我的直觉，还是说现在的新闻确实比比如说10年前要多得多、多得多？

sentences.en: Dr. Grant is a media psychologiSt. What are your thoughts on this?
sentences.zh: 格兰特博士是一位媒体心理学家。你对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: Certainly, I don't know that there's any more information or news happening.
sentences.zh: 当然，我不知道是不是真的有更多信息或新闻发生。

sentences.en: The difference, in my opinion, is how it's delivered, because maybe dating myself, but back when I was growing up, we had a television, a radio, and newspapers.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，区别在于它的传播方式，因为也许这暴露了我的年龄，但在我成长的时候，我们只有电视、收音机和报纸。

sentences.en: Now we have the internet, and we've got increasingly more platforms, all clamoring to get our attention with sensationalized headlines, again, in my opinion, on the same topic.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有了互联网，而且我们拥有越来越多的平台，它们都以哗众取宠的标题来争夺我们的注意力，在我看来，这都是围绕着同一个话题。

sentences.en: My opinion is the inflection point happened in 2008.
sentences.zh: 我的看法是，转折点发生在2008年。

sentences.en: In 2008, Apple introduced the iPhone, which made the internet portable.
sentences.zh: 2008年，苹果推出了iPhone，让互联网变得便携。

sentences.en: So once we had the news conduit, or the information, or whatever it was, when the internet went
sentences.zh: 所以一旦我们有了新闻渠道、信息或其他什么，当互联网变得

sentences.en: portable, in my opinion, that was when we crossed the event horizon, and now it is always, always
sentences.zh: 便携时，在我看来，那就是我们跨越事件视界的时候，现在它总是、随时随地

sentences.en: available, and we have alerts, and notifications, and the constant checking, and I'm sure Dr.
sentences.zh: 可用，我们有警报、通知，还有不断地查看，我确信布劳恩博士

sentences.en: Barrow can speak about this more.
sentences.zh: 可以对此发表更多看法。

sentences.en: But that's really, I don't think there's more news.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我不认为有更多的新闻。

sentences.en: I just think that we've got more accessibility to it, and we've got increasingly more platforms that are just all trying to get our attention to read about it.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为我们对它的可访问性更高了，我们有了越来越多的平台，它们都在试图吸引我们的注意力去阅读它。

sentences.en: So let me ask them, what's the impact, both psychological and physiological, of exposure to so much news, and so much of it being negative?
sentences.zh: 那么请问，接触如此之多且大部分是负面的新闻，会带来什么心理和生理上的影响？

sentences.en: Maybe news has always been negative, but it just feels even more so today.
sentences.zh: 也许新闻一直都是负面的，但现在感觉更加严重了。

sentences.en: Dr. Barrow, maybe you could talk about your study findings, because I think you looked at some of this.
sentences.zh: 布劳恩博士，也许你可以谈谈你的研究发现，因为我想你研究过其中的一些内容。

sentences.en: I can.
sentences.zh: 我可以。

sentences.en: I don't think that it's just there's an impact of more news, and that that impact is negative.
sentences.zh: 我不认为仅仅是新闻更多了产生影响，并且这种影响是负面的。

sentences.en: The news themselves also have changed, right?
sentences.zh: 新闻本身也变了，对吧？

sentences.en: Dr. Grant just talked about sensationalism, and how the greater competition leads actually to different types of news being reported.
sentences.zh: 格兰特博士刚才谈到了耸人听闻的现象，以及激烈的竞争实际上如何导致不同类型的新闻被报道。

sentences.en: So it's not just more, it's also a different kind of information that is being communicated.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是更多，也是正在传播的不同种类的信息。

sentences.en: And I think that's what has the detrimental effects.
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是产生有害影响的原因。

sentences.en: So let me talk about these detrimental effects.
sentences.zh: 那么我来谈谈这些有害影响。

sentences.en: We did that study
sentences.zh: 我们做的那项研究

sentences.en: where we asked people about their news consumption, both on social media, television, and also newspapers,
sentences.zh: 询问了人们关于他们在社交媒体、电视以及报纸上的新闻消费情况，

sentences.en: and where do they get their news from, and how much time do they spend consuming, consulting these different sources.
sentences.zh: 以及他们从哪里获取新闻，以及他们花多少时间消费、查阅这些不同的来源。

sentences.en: And then we also measured their emotional distress, self-reported emotional distress.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还测量了他们的情绪困扰，自我报告的情绪困扰。

sentences.en: And we found a positive correlation between news consumption and emotional distress.
sentences.zh: 我们发现新闻消费与情绪困扰之间存在正相关关系。

sentences.en: It wasn't entirely surprising, the social media, we know with algorithms, those that get more click, have a little more negative
sentences.zh: 这并不完全令人惊讶，对于社交媒体，我们知道通过算法，那些获得更多点击量的会带有更多一点负面

sentences.en: news, and people report negative events more, they get shared more often.
sentences.zh: 新闻，人们更多地报告负面事件，它们被分享得更频繁。

sentences.en: So all these algorithms sort of contribute to more negative news being shared on social media.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些算法某种程度上促使更多负面新闻在社交媒体上被分享。

sentences.en: I have to admit that we were a little surprised by the positive relationship between emotional distress and newspaper consumptions.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，对于情绪困扰与报纸消费之间的正向关系，我们感到有点惊讶。

sentences.en: We somehow thought, especially in the early days of COVID-19, we thought that inform newspapers, facts, um, knowledge about infection risk.
sentences.zh: 我们不知为何认为，尤其是在COVID-19的早期阶段，我们认为知情报纸、事实，嗯，关于感染风险的知识。

sentences.en: What is, what do we know?
sentences.zh: 什么是，我们知道什么？

sentences.en: What do we not know?
sentences.zh: 我们不知道什么？

sentences.en: What is true?
sentences.zh: 什么是真的？

sentences.en: What is not true?
sentences.zh: 什么不是真的？

sentences.en: We thought that that would actually reduce emotional distress.
sentences.zh: 我们曾认为这实际上会减少情绪困扰。

sentences.en: Well, we found exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们发现的情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It increased emotional distress.
sentences.zh: 它增加了情绪困扰。

sentences.en: Do you have any idea why?
sentences.zh: 你们知道为什么吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I was going to ask at some point whether the medium matters, and it would seem to me that reading a newspaper, the imagery is more in your mind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我曾一度想问媒介是否重要，在我看来，阅读报纸时，意象更多地存在于你的脑海中。

sentences.en: I mean, there are some pictures, but you do have to imagine things as opposed to when you're watching TV or even seeing a video on, on the internet.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一些图片，但与看电视甚至看网上的视频相比，你确实必须自己去想象。

sentences.en: So what's the difference here?
sentences.zh: 所以这里的区别是什么？

sentences.en: I think there are about five or 10 causes that may be responsible for this difference.
sentences.zh: 我认为大约有五到十个原因可能导致这种差异。

sentences.en: It's definitely the case that we found the strongest correlation between emotional distress and news consumption on social media.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，我们发现情绪困扰与社交媒体上的新闻消费之间存在最强的相关性。

sentences.en: It's definitely true that the weakest correlation was between emotional distress and newspaper consumption.
sentences.zh: 绝对没错，最弱的相关性存在于情绪困扰与报纸消费之间。

sentences.en: It was the weakest, but it was still positive, and it was still statistically significant.
sentences.zh: 它是最弱的，但它仍然是正相关的，并且在统计学上仍然是显著的。

sentences.en: The more somebody spent time reading newspaper articles related to COVID-19, the more emotionally distressed they felt.
sentences.zh: 一个人花在阅读与COVID-19相关的报纸文章上的时间越多，他们感到情绪困扰的程度就越高。

sentences.en: It is interesting to see this relationship, and we can only wonder what it is due to.
sentences.zh: 看到这种关系很有趣，我们只能猜测这是由于什么原因。

sentences.en: I mean, once again, I actually think that even newspaper journalists are subject to that competition that Dr. Grant pointed out before.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，再说一次，我其实认为连报纸记者也受到格兰特博士之前指出的那种竞争的影响。

sentences.en: Nowadays, many of the newspapers, New York Times, have online versions.
sentences.zh: 如今，许多报纸，比如《纽约时报》，都有网络版。

sentences.en: And here, it's the number of clicks.
sentences.zh: 在这里，关键在于点击量。

sentences.en: And a journalist that writes articles that generates many clicks, their career will advance faster than that of a journalist whose articles have few clicks.
sentences.zh: 一个撰写能产生大量点击量的文章的记者，其职业生涯的发展速度会比那些文章点击量很少的记者更快。

sentences.en: So I think even journalists in news media are subject to the competition and the incentive structure that are such to report more negative news and more sensational news.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，即使是新闻媒体中的记者也受制于竞争和激励结构，这些结构倾向于报道更多负面新闻和更加耸人听闻的新闻。

sentences.en: So then let me ask you, Dr. Grant, is some of the blame for this then lies at the feet of
sentences.zh: 那么我想问你，格兰特博士，这其中的部分责任是否在于

sentences.en: reporters or their editors and producers, that they're just being goaded into basically producing more sensationalistic and even more negative news?
sentences.zh: 记者或他们的编辑和制片人，因为他们只是被逼着去制作更多耸人听闻甚至更负面的新闻？

sentences.en: I wouldn't use the word blame necessarily, but I want to take it back.
sentences.zh: 我不一定会用“责怪”这个词，但我想把它拉回来。

sentences.en: We did a study, which was super interesting.
sentences.zh: 我们做了一项研究，超级有趣。

sentences.en: We looked at one news story.
sentences.zh: 我们看了一则新闻报道。

sentences.en: We just picked one.
sentences.zh: 我们随便挑了一则。

sentences.en: And we looked at how news platforms around the world, because we wanted external validity, of course.
sentences.zh: 我们观察了世界各地的新闻平台是如何报道的，因为我们当然需要外部效度。

sentences.en: So we looked at how they promoted and reported this one story, including the byline, the, you know, the title in the byline.
sentences.zh: 所以我们研究了他们如何推广和报道这则新闻，包括署名，你知道的，署名里的标题。

sentences.en: It was fascinating to see the same story.
sentences.zh: 看到同一则新闻非常吸引人。

sentences.en: And when you, when it came up in the feeds, how it was the, you know, because it used to be top of the fold, right?
sentences.zh: 当你在动态中看到它时，它是如何成为，你知道的，因为以前是头版头条，对吧？

sentences.en: In newspapers and whoever had top of the fold and anyone's familiar with that term, it was whatever was on the front page.
sentences.zh: 在报纸上，谁能占头版头条，熟悉这个词的人都知道，那就是头版上的任何内容。

sentences.en: The front page now is one line, maybe six words on an internet search or on a feed.
sentences.zh: 现在的头版是一行字，在互联网搜索或动态中可能只有六个词。

sentences.en: So I also want to be fair, and I agree with everything.
sentences.zh: 所以我也想保持公平，我同意所有观点。

sentences.en: I think where we're going, and we can talk about this more, and Dr. Broward obviously has the research.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们正在走向的方向，我们可以对此做更多讨论，布劳尔博士显然有相关的研究。

sentences.en: I have to look at that, Dr. Broward.
sentences.zh: 我得看看那个，布劳尔博士。

sentences.en: That's really fascinating to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说真的很有趣。

sentences.en: You could see a story in a newspaper or on the news, which we trusted.
sentences.zh: 你可以在报纸或新闻上看到一则我们信任的故事。

sentences.en: Now, keeping in mind, there's controversy over the years about who controlled newspapers and media.
sentences.zh: 现在，请记住，多年来关于谁控制报纸和媒体一直存在争议。

sentences.en: But let's just remove that.
sentences.zh: 但我们先抛开这个不谈。

sentences.en: That's a different podcast, maybe.
sentences.zh: 那也许是另一期播客的内容。

sentences.en: We trusted that what we saw was fact check.
sentences.zh: 我们相信我们看到的是经过事实核查的。

sentences.en: It was correct.
sentences.zh: 它是正确的。

sentences.en: I did an interview.
sentences.zh: 我做过一次采访。

sentences.en: I was very fortunate.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运。

sentences.en: I did an interview for a very prestigious newspaper on Monday, and they sent me fact checks later.
sentences.zh: 我在周一为一家非常著名的报纸接受了一次采访，他们后来给我发送了事实核查。

sentences.en: But I also want to remind us that as we would maybe that morning read something in a newspaper or hear it on one of the news stations
sentences.zh: 但我也想提醒大家，正如我们可能那天早上在报纸上读到或在我们信任的新闻台之一听到

sentences.en: that we trusted, we go to the market, and we're standing in line.
sentences.zh: 我们去市场，正排着队。

sentences.en: And there are four or five different, they called them tabloids.
sentences.zh: 那里有四五种不同的杂志，他们称之为小报。

sentences.en: Maybe it had the same story.
sentences.zh: 也许它有相同的故事。

sentences.en: But what we saw on the cover was a very different lensing of it.
sentences.zh: 但我们在封面看到的是一种非常不同的视角。

sentences.en: So it's not like, I don't think it's new.
sentences.zh: 所以这不像，我不认为这是新鲜事。

sentences.en: I think that it's what Dr. Brower said.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是布劳尔博士所说的。

sentences.en: And what I believe is that everyone, you know, is ambitious.
sentences.zh: 而且我相信每个人，你知道的，都是有雄心的。

sentences.en: We all want our careers to do well.
sentences.zh: 我们都希望自己的职业生涯发展顺利。

sentences.en: And I don't know that they're purposely trying.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们是不是故意这样做的。

sentences.en: But when you have increasingly more news platforms that are digitally delivered, all trying to get your eyes on it and to, as Dr.
sentences.zh: 但当你拥有越来越多数字发布的新闻平台，它们都试图吸引你的眼球，正如布劳尔

sentences.en: Brower said, click on it.
sentences.zh: 博士所说，点击它。

sentences.en: You are going to try to do something that is going to be alluring, attractive and get them to click the same as I live in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 你会尝试做一些诱人、有吸引力的事情，让他们点击，就像我住在洛杉矶一样。

sentences.en: And there's certain metropolitan areas that had back in the day, two newspapers, or more.
sentences.zh: 有些大都市区过去曾有两家或更多报纸。

sentences.en: So in certain urban areas, this is not, you know, a new practice where competing newspapers in the same market, I think
sentences.zh: 所以在某些城市地区，这并不是，你知道的，什么新鲜做法，在同一市场上的竞争报纸，我认为

sentences.en: probably had discussions about how to have people, you know, look at theirs of the same story.
sentences.zh: 可能讨论过如何让人们，你知道的，在同一则新闻中看他们自己的那份。

sentences.en: So I don't know that it's blaming, I just think that it's now, you know, we've got they've got six words,
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道这算不算责怪，我只是认为现在，你知道的，他们有六个词，

sentences.en: maybe ellipses, ellipses, when you look at a newsfeeder, you Google something to grab your attention and get you to click on that.
sentences.zh: 也许是省略号，当你看着新闻流时，你用谷歌搜索某些东西来吸引你的注意力并让你点击它。

sentences.en: So you do so that the journalists get the clicks.
sentences.zh: 你这样做是为了让记者获得点击量。

sentences.en: And I work with, I, cause what happens is creators put things up there and then people respond and come at them.
sentences.zh: 我和……合作，我，因为发生的情况是创作者把东西放到那里，然后人们做出回应并针对他们。

sentences.en: And so I, uh, when we were talking about being lost in the vortex, I can't even tell you how many times I've sat with a client who has
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，当我们谈论迷失在漩涡中时，我简直无法告诉你我有多少次和一个客户坐在一起，他们的

sentences.en: their sleep hygiene has been disrupted by YouTube.
sentences.zh: 睡眠卫生被 YouTube 破坏了。

sentences.en: They've been up all night and I asked them quite frankly.
sentences.zh: 他们一整夜没睡，我直言不讳地问他们。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Can you tell me just one video?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我哪怕一个视频吗？

sentences.en: What did you see?
sentences.zh: 你看到了什么？

sentences.en: It is shocking to me.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: The phenomenon to a one, they can't remember one video and they were up all night.
sentences.zh: 这种现象是，无一例外，他们记不清一个视频，而他们通宵未眠。

sentences.en: So when you talk about how it impacts those different silos.
sentences.zh: 所以当你谈论它如何影响这些不同的领域时。

sentences.en: And again, Dr. Brower can speak to this much better than me.
sentences.zh: 再次声明，布劳尔（Brower）博士可以比我更好地谈论这一点。

sentences.en: I just have kitchen table experience of dealing with kids and family for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 我只有 20 年来处理儿童和家庭问题的厨房餐桌经验。

sentences.en: And, and through this whole, uh, rise of the internet and, and, uh, the digital, the portable digital use, but that's what I got.
sentences.zh: 而且，通过这整个，呃，互联网的兴起，以及，呃，数字、便携式数字设备的使用，这就是我的全部经验。

sentences.en: Dr. Brower, what's your opinion here?
sentences.zh: 布劳尔博士，你有什么看法？

sentences.en: Do you agree?
sentences.zh: 你同意吗？

sentences.en: And, and do we need to have something in the DSM that, you know, really flags this as, as a serious, serious problem?
sentences.zh: 而且，我们是否需要在 DSM 中加入一些内容，你知道，真正将这标记为一个极其严重的问题？

sentences.en: Dr. Brower, I'm actually interested in what, cause I respect what you would call it.
sentences.zh: 布劳尔博士，我其实对你的看法很感兴趣，因为我很尊重你会怎么称呼它。

sentences.en: Dr. Brower, I have no idea, media addiction or some syndrome, but it's, it's, it's going to be tough to do that.
sentences.zh: 布劳尔博士，我不知道，媒体成瘾或某种综合征，但这，这，这做起来会很难。

sentences.en: Uh, partly because it's correlated with so many other things in the, all the causal directions going all in, in, in all, all the causal effects go in all directions.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于它与许多其他事情相关联，所有的因果方向都指向四面八方。

sentences.en: So on the one hand, we know that social media consumption leads to poor mental health, right?
sentences.zh: 一方面，我们知道社交媒体消费会导致糟糕的心理健康，对吧？

sentences.en: Everybody else seems to be having fun.
sentences.zh: 其他人似乎都玩得很开心。

sentences.en: Everybody else is on these great vacations and I'm not terrible fear of missing out.
sentences.zh: 其他人都在进行精彩的度假，而我却没有——对错失的巨大恐惧（FOMO）。

sentences.en: So I'm sorry to interrupt you.
sentences.zh: 所以很抱歉打断你。

sentences.en: I call that compare and despair, compare and despair.
sentences.zh: 我称之为“比较与绝望”（compare and despair）。

sentences.en: So it leads to poor mental health, but also, uh, sometimes social media use are indicators of other clinical, uh, problems, right?
sentences.zh: 所以它会导致糟糕的心理健康，但同时，嗯，有时社交媒体的使用也是其他临床，嗯，问题的指标，对吧？

sentences.en: Loneliness, uh, social awkwardness, uh, inability to connect, uh, no close social, uh, uh, um, support network, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 孤独、嗯，社交尴尬、嗯，无法建立连接、嗯，没有紧密的社交，嗯，嗯，支持网络等。

sentences.en: So, uh, the, the, the correlations, the relationships with other clinical, uh, issues are, um, um, uh, are close and it's going to be hard to distinguish it from that.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，与，与，与其他临床，嗯，问题的相关性，关系是，嗯，嗯，很紧密的，很难将它与那些区分开来。

sentences.en: And so, um, I want to move to something slightly different.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，我想转向一个稍微不同的主题。

sentences.en: Yes, we, maybe we need a clinical diagnosis, but we can also sort of in the meantime, work on making things better.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们，也许我们需要一个临床诊断，但与此同时，我们也可以着手让情况变得更好。

sentences.en: I think much of it is raising awareness in the public or maybe among our teenagers.
sentences.zh: 我认为很大程度上是在公众中提高意识，或者也许在我们的青少年中提高意识。

sentences.en: So we already talked about how hardwired we are, uh, for negative events.
sentences.zh: 所以我们刚才已经讨论过了，我们对负面事件的神经连线有多深，嗯。

sentences.en: Um, we just talked about how these social media platforms, uh, feed us, uh, information that is negative and that make us come back and what their ultimate goal is.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚讨论了这些社交媒体平台，嗯，如何向我们喂食，嗯，负面的信息，并让我们不断回访，以及它们的最终目标是什么。

sentences.en: I think also it should be made quite clear that people are very bad at distinguishing real,
sentences.zh: 我认为还应该非常明确地指出，人们非常不善于区分真实的，

sentences.en: distinguishing real news from fake news and people widely exaggerate, uh, overestimate their ability to do that.
sentences.zh: 区分真实新闻和假新闻，而且人们极大地夸大了，嗯，高估了他们这样做的能力。

sentences.en: We're actually incredibly poor and there are hundreds of studies showing exactly that, that, uh, what is on there.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上差得难以置信，有数百项研究准确地显示了这一点，即，嗯，上面的内容。

sentences.en: And even if it's a little video and if, even if it's people with a white coat standing on the stairs of the Capitol, that does not mean that that is actually, uh,
sentences.zh: 即使是一个小视频，即使是穿白大褂的人站在国会大厦的台阶上，这并不意味着这实际上是，嗯，

sentences.en: official information and has any value.
sentences.zh: 官方信息，并具有任何价值。

sentences.en: So we are very, uh, bad at judging, distinguishing fake news from, from real news.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常，嗯，不善于判断、区分假新闻和真实新闻。

sentences.en: And finally, I think what we need is a little bit more training, uh, maybe statistical thinking or being able to understand uncertainty and, uh, um, what it means like to
sentences.zh: 最后，我认为我们需要的是更多一点的训练，嗯，也许是统计思维，或者能够理解不确定性以及，嗯，嗯，这意味着什么，

sentences.en: take, take, come back to the study was the initial weeks of COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 回到那个研究，那是 2019 冠状病毒病（COVID-19）最初的几周。

sentences.en: We didn't really know, uh, what was going on, but certain pieces of information were more reliable than others.
sentences.zh: 我们当时并不是真的很清楚，嗯，发生了什么，但某些信息比其他信息更可靠。

sentences.en: And we knew more about that.
sentences.zh: 我们对此了解更多。

sentences.en: So at this stage, um, we now think it might be airborne.
sentences.zh: 所以在现阶段，嗯，我们现在认为它可能是通过空气传播的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That is, um, an uncertain judgment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个，嗯，不确定的判断。

sentences.en: And then now it's 99% sure that it's airborne and that's actually, that's how the transmission works and we can stop disinfecting our groceries.
sentences.zh: 然后现在有 99% 的把握确定它是通过空气传播的，实际上，这就是传播的方式，我们可以停止对杂货进行消毒了。

sentences.en: Um, uh, teaching people to sort of, um, read through the lines and what is reliable information and what is unreliable information.
sentences.zh: 嗯，嗯，教导人们去，嗯，字里行间领会，什么是可靠信息，什么是不可靠信息。

sentences.en: And then maybe the next step is where do you get that information?
sentences.zh: 然后也许下一步就是你在哪里获取这些信息？

sentences.en: Maybe social media is not the right place to get that information.
sentences.zh: 也许社交媒体并不是获取这些信息的正确地方。

sentences.en: Maybe you should be going on the website.
sentences.zh: 也许你应该去网站上查找。

sentences.en: If you really want to know about infection risk and what we currently know, maybe the CDC website is, is the better, or every state has a health department.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想了解感染风险以及我们目前所了解的情况，也许疾控中心（CDC）的网站是更好的选择，或者每个州都有卫生部门。

sentences.en: And they're now making a real effort to, um, provide information for, um, non-experts, non-scientists, sometimes even for kids, adolescents.
sentences.zh: 他们现在正做出真正的努力，嗯，为，嗯，非专家、非科学家，有时甚至为儿童、青少年提供信息。

sentences.en: So I think, um, maybe we should teach our, especially our teenagers, uh, and, and friends.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，嗯，也许我们应该教导我们的，特别是我们的青少年，嗯，和，和朋友。

sentences.en: Um, we go to different sources for different things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们针对不同的事情去不同的渠道。

sentences.en: I think we go to social media to watch cute animal videos and they make us feel good.
sentences.zh: 我想我们去社交媒体是为了看可爱的动物视频，它们让我们感觉良好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then that's okay.
sentences.zh: 然后这就对了。

sentences.en: And then if we want to know what the infection risk is and how I can minimize that and actually whether I should go to my
sentences.zh: 然后如果我们想知道感染风险是什么，以及我如何将其降到最低，实际上我是否应该在新冠疫情期间去参加

sentences.en: grandfather's 85th birthday in the time of COVID, I think the CDC website might be the better source than social media.
sentences.zh: 我祖父的 85 岁生日，我认为疾控中心网站可能是比社交媒体更好的信息源。

sentences.en: I agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我同意这一点。

sentences.en: You know, I teach healthy device management in the practice of good digital citizenship.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在实践中教授健康的设备管理和良好的数字公民意识。

sentences.en: If you look at the reason why ostensibly we even seek out news sources, it's to get information that we don't have, or we don't know, and to learn as humans.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看我们表面上甚至寻找新闻来源的原因，它是为了获取我们没有的信息，或者我们不知道的信息，并作为人类去学习。

sentences.en: I fear that what I'm seeing and what I believe in our psychology and our fear-based, you know, belief system, we tend to believe people who say things that align with what we feel.
sentences.zh: 我担心我所看到的以及我相信在我们的心理学和基于恐惧的，你知道，信仰系统中，我们倾向于相信那些说的话符合我们感受的人。

sentences.en: We're not really as interested in learning from the other side.
sentences.zh: 我们其实对向另一方学习不那么感兴趣。

sentences.en: So right now you can find anything, something that aligns with your belief system, whether it's whatever, but you can find people.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你可以找到任何东西，找到符合你信仰系统的东西，不管是哪种，但你能找到这样的人。

sentences.en: And I love that Dr. Barr said the white coat.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴布尔（Barr）博士提到了白大褂。

sentences.en: Anyone can put on a white coat and we're used to believing what they say, but I think that we are so used to, uh, we will follow.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以穿上白大褂，我们习惯于相信他们所说的话，但我认为我们太习惯于，嗯，我们会追随。

sentences.en: And I mean that in both ways, both in terms of the definition that it was traditional and also now with, with, uh, social media, we'll follow people who kind of say things
sentences.zh: 我的意思是双重的，既指传统意义上的定义，也指现在，随着，嗯，社交媒体的发展，我们会追随那些说的话

sentences.en: that make sense and aligns with our beliefs.
sentences.zh: 讲得通并且符合我们信仰的人。

sentences.en: I don't know if we're really interested in learning new things.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们是否真的对学习新事物感兴趣。

sentences.en: And the idea that we then can share that with others and it can just grow and grow and grow and grow.
sentences.zh: 以及这样一种想法，即然后我们可以与他人分享这一点，它可以不断增长、增长、增长、增长。

sentences.en: And then hit a groundswell of suddenly you have these cabals of, of people sharing misinformation.
sentences.zh: 然后形成一股声势，突然之间你就会有这些分享错误信息的阴谋小集团。

sentences.en: This is something again, that's new.
sentences.zh: 这同样是新出现的东西。

sentences.en: And what Dr. Brower said is something I'm very interested in.
sentences.zh: 布劳尔博士所说的话正是我非常感兴趣的。

sentences.en: I'm doing right now.
sentences.zh: 我目前正在这样做。

sentences.en: Critical thinking, critical thinking is something that we are very trained to do.
sentences.zh: 批判性思维，批判性思维是我们经过大量训练去做的事情。

sentences.en: I remember my mentor explaining to me when I first was going and pursuing this, that Wikipedia is not a citable source.
sentences.zh: 我记得我的导师在我刚开始从事和追求这个领域时向我解释，维基百科不是一个可引用的来源。

sentences.en: I didn't know.
sentences.zh: 我当时并不知道。

sentences.en: So, uh, critical thinking.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，批判性思维。

sentences.en: And I think it's very important that we have policies just like everything we've added in,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，制定相应的政策非常重要，就像我们添加的所有内容一样，

sentences.en: just like what's going on now with inclusion and diversity, as we grow and evolve and become more sentient and kinder and, and more open-minded.
sentences.zh: 就像现在关于包容性和多样性的进展一样，随着我们的成长和演变，变得更有感知力、更善良、也更开明。

sentences.en: I think that it is vital that we do not avoid this.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们绝对不能回避这一点，这一点至关重要。

sentences.en: And that in the curriculum, starting young before they even get on devices, I think that critical thinking and device, healthy device management and good digital citizenship.
sentences.zh: 并且在课程中，在他们甚至还没接触电子设备的小时候就开始，我认为批判性思维以及健康的设备管理和良好的数字公民意识。

sentences.en: I think these should be de-rigueur protocol curriculum pieces because we need to get ahead of it before the kids actually get on the device.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些应该成为必不可少的协议课程，因为我们需要在孩子们真正接触设备之前抢先一步。

sentences.en: And I tell parents, uh, you know, whatever, and I talk about good, good digital citizenship.
sentences.zh: 我告诉家长们，呃，你知道，无论如何，我都会谈论良好的数字公民意识。

sentences.en: And this is again with cyber bullying and other trolling things that we've now seen.
sentences.zh: 这再次涉及到我们现在所看到的网络霸凌和其他骂战等现象。

sentences.en: Uh, I tell parents, here's the basic thing that I suggest before you let your children have that
sentences.zh: 呃，我告诉家长们，这是我建议的基本原则：在你们允许孩子拥有那个

sentences.en: privilege of that device, which you're paying for, sit down with them and discuss what are your family values of how you treat people IRL in real life.
sentences.zh: 由你们付费购买的设备这一特权之前，先坐下来和他们讨论，明确你们的家庭价值观：在现实生活中你们是如何对待别人的。

sentences.en: And that absolutely the expectation of how it should translate online.
sentences.zh: 并且这完全应该体现在网络世界的行为准则中。

sentences.en: But I think that if we don't put this kind of curriculum and educate kids and the community and parents and what we're doing right now, this is the good use of all this
sentences.zh: 但我认为，如果我们不设立这种课程，不教育孩子、社区和家长，不去做我们现在正在做的事情——也就是充分利用所有这些

sentences.en: digital media, your show, Kim, this can reach people.
sentences.zh: 数字媒体，金，你的节目就能触达大众。

sentences.en: I don't know who's going to be listening to this, but maybe they heard something, but I think that this should be de-rigueur protocol
sentences.zh: 我不知道谁会收听这个节目，但也许他们听到了一些内容，不过我认为这应该成为必不可少的准则：

sentences.en: of critical thinking, discerning information, where to find sources that are, uh, you know, that are trusted.
sentences.zh: 批判性思维、辨别信息、以及去哪里寻找呃，你知道的，值得信赖的信息源。

sentences.en: And this should be a part of school curriculum because this is a part of our kids' everyday life.
sentences.zh: 这应该成为学校课程的一部分，因为这是我们孩子们日常生活的一部分。

sentences.en: It's when, once we go into virtual reality, augmented reality, mixture of whatever AI, whatever's coming, why don't we have this in the schools?
sentences.zh: 当，一旦我们进入虚拟现实、增强现实、各种人工智能的混合体、或是未来迎面而来的任何事物时，为什么我们不在学校里开设这些呢？

sentences.en: Because they're going to use this probably more than calculus, the kids, because now they don't need calculus because they can just ask Surrey to solve the problem for them.
sentences.zh: 因为孩子们使用这些的频率可能比微积分还要高，因为现在他们根本不需要学微积分，直接让Siri帮他们解题就行了。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to have to thank you both.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我要谢谢你们两位。

sentences.en: I think this is fascinating and we could probably go on for, for another hour and still have new things to say
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个话题非常吸引人，我们大概还能再聊一个小时，而且还会有说不完的新内容，

sentences.en: because this is such a hot area, but I want to thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个如此热门的领域，但我要感谢你们今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好，谢谢你们。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Kim.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，金。
